title: Sets that Support a Joint Distribution
summary: Given probability distributions $μ$ and $ν$ on measure spaces $X$ and $Y$, and a closed set $S \subseteq X \times Y$, when is there a probability distribution on $X \times Y$ whose marginals are $μ$ and $ν$, and whose support is precisely $S$? We answer the question when the marginals are discrete, and when the marginals are continuous distributions on the real line. Of special interest is the case where $S \subseteq [0,1]^2$ and $μ$ and $ν$ are Lebesgue measure; then the above question is tantamount to ``when is $S$ the support of a doubly stochastic measure?".
